clinical_knowledge.topic: Bipolar I Disorder (Manic Episode) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Bipolar I Disorder (Manic Episode) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

A manic episode requires at least one week of abnormally elevated, expansive, or irritable mood and increased energy with associated symptoms and marked impairment, hospitalization, or psychosis; assess for substances, medications, and medical or neurologic causes.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, grandiosity

Key HPI features: A 32-year-old female presents after 7 days of decreased need for sleep with sustained energy, pressured speech, grandiosity, and escalating impulsive behavior causing marked impairment.

Objective/Exam findings: Obtain vital signs, hydration status, focused neurologic and mental-status examination, including psychosis, insight, judgment, capacity, and suicide, self-harm, violence, vulnerability, and inability-to-care-for-self risk.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Bipolar I Disorder (Manic Episode).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Schizoaffective disorder without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging a patient with impaired judgment, psychosis, or inability to participate in a safe discharge plan; use local involuntary-treatment procedures when criteria are met.
Missing intoxication, stimulant use, medication-induced mania, delirium, hyperthyroidism, or neurologic illness as mimics or contributors.

Starting lithium or valproate without baseline renal, thyroid, hepatic, hematologic, metabolic, interaction, and pregnancy assessment as applicable; valproate has major fetal risk and requires explicit pregnancy-prevention counseling where relevant.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Severe impulse control loss (reckless spending/driving).
management_principles: Urgently assess danger to self or others, grave disability, capacity, ability to consent, and need for emergency psychiatric evaluation or involuntary admission under local law; obtain collateral when appropriate.
Admit to a psychiatric inpatient unit; use a low-stimulation setting, protect sleep and hydration, and restrict access to money, vehicles, and other foreseeable hazards.

Obtain CBC, CMP including renal and hepatic function and calcium, TSH, urine toxicology, blood alcohol level when indicated, ECG, and pregnancy test before teratogenic medicines when applicable. Initiate an antipsychotic and mood stabilizer per local protocol, with required drug-level, laboratory, metabolic, and adverse-effect monitoring.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 32-year-old woman with seven days of reduced need for sleep, sustained energy, pressured speech, grandiosity, escalating impulsive behavior, and marked impairment. Assess all manic symptoms, psychosis, prior mood episodes, substances/medications, medical or neurologic symptoms, collateral history, capacity, and suicide, self-harm, violence, vulnerability, and inability-to-care-for-self risk.
reference_soap.objective: Obtain vital signs, hydration status, focused neurologic and mental-status examination, and targeted studies including CBC, CMP with renal/hepatic function and calcium, TSH, toxicology, alcohol testing when indicated, ECG, and pregnancy testing before teratogenic medicines when applicable.
reference_soap.assessment: Manic episode with marked impairment, concerning for Bipolar I disorder; exclude substance/medication-induced and medical causes and characterize psychotic features and immediate risk.
reference_soap.plan: Urgent psychiatric evaluation and inpatient admission; determine whether involuntary treatment criteria apply under local law. Use a low-stimulation setting, restore sleep and hydration, obtain collateral, and restrict foreseeable financial and driving risks. Initiate an antipsychotic and mood stabilizer per local protocol after baseline testing. Monitor serum levels and renal/thyroid function for lithium, hepatic/hematologic effects for valproate, and metabolic/neurologic adverse effects for antipsychotics. Discuss valproate's major fetal risk and pregnancy prevention when relevant.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Bipolar I manic
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Bipolar I manic
Implement evidence-based management plan: Admit for safety, start Valproate or Lithium and Olanzapine

teaching.one_liner: At least one week of abnormally elevated, expansive, or irritable mood with increased energy, associated manic symptoms, and marked impairment, hospitalization, or psychosis.
red_flags: Suicide, self-harm, violence, vulnerability, inability to care for self, or impaired capacity
Delirium, intoxication, substance withdrawal, or rapidly changing consciousness

must_ask.say: Do you feel full of energy even after sleeping only two or three hours?
Does your mind feel like it is racing so fast that your words cannot keep up?
Do you feel you have special powers, famous connections, or a divine mission?
Have you engaged in risky spending sprees, reckless driving, or risky sexual choices?
Have you also experienced severe depressive crashes in the past?
Are you having thoughts of suicide, harming yourself or anyone else, or do you feel unable to keep yourself safe? Is there someone we can contact to help us make a safe plan?
Have you used alcohol, cannabis, stimulants, or other drugs, stopped any substances suddenly, or started medicines such as antidepressants or steroids?

history.answer: I haven't slept more than an hour or two a night for the past week, but I feel completely wired and my mind and mouth won't stop racing.
It started about seven days ago quite suddenly, and my energy and ideas have been ramping up continuously every single day.
I've only been sleeping one or two hours each night, yet I jump out of bed feeling 100 percent energized and ready to take on the world.
I feel fantastic, completely euphoric and invincible, but I get very irritable and frustrated when other people tell me to slow down or calm down.
My thoughts are flying by so fast it feels like fireworks in my brain, and I just have an overwhelming urge to keep talking so I don't lose them.
I think my brain has just unlocked this incredible burst of creative power, so I don't even need regular sleep right now.
I spent over five thousand dollars of my savings online buying top-tier electronics and designer clothes, and I've been driving much faster than usual because I felt in complete control.
No, I haven't heard any voices talking to me or commenting on what I do, and I haven't seen anything unusual or unreal.
No, there are no voices ordering me to do anything.
No one is spying on me, following me, or putting thoughts into my head, and my thoughts aren't leaking out; I just feel unusually gifted.
No, I've never experienced strange beliefs, paranoia, or hallucinations at times when my mood was normal.
About two years ago, I had a period of about three weeks where I felt terribly down, exhausted, couldn't get out of bed, and lost interest in everything.
No, absolutely not. I don't want to hurt or kill myself at all; I feel too full of life right now.
No, I don't have any thoughts of harming anyone and I don't carry any weapons, though I did shout at my sister when she tried to take my car keys.
I haven't really eaten full meals or showered much because I've been so obsessed with working on my ideas, and I've missed three days of work.
Deep down I know this speed isn't sustainable and I wondered if this could be mania like bipolar, so I came in wanting a proper evaluation and help.

history.answer: I'm worried that my family is going to hold me back and ruin the huge new projects I'm trying to launch. I just want you to sign off that I'm completely fine so my family will stop bothering me and let me work.
My sister was really worried about my spending and drove me here today; she's in the waiting room and you have my full permission to speak with her.
I had a busy project deadline at work last month, but nothing traumatic or unusual happened right before this started.
No, I have never used methamphetamine, cocaine, cannabis, amphetamines, steroids, or any other recreational drugs.
I have never been diagnosed with a psychiatric condition before, so I've never been on mood stabilizers, antidepressants, or antipsychotics.
No, I haven't had any headaches, seizures, episodes of confusion, fevers, heart palpitations, or unexplained weight loss.
No, I have never had a baby and I haven't been pregnant recently.
I don't have any chronic medical conditions, no thyroid problems, and no history of head injuries.
I've never had any operations and I've never been admitted to a hospital.
I'm not taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter medicines, or dietary supplements.
I don't have any known allergies to medications, foods, or anything else.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used e-cigarettes.
I only drink a glass of wine occasionally when socialising, and I haven't had any alcohol over the last two weeks.
I work as a graphic designer and I live by myself in an apartment, but my sister lives only ten minutes away.
My mother has suffered from recurrent major depression, and my maternal aunt was diagnosed with bipolar disorder.
My sex drive has felt much higher this past week, but I haven't had any risky, unprotected, or new sexual encounters.
My last menstrual period was two weeks ago, my cycles are regular every 28 days, I use condoms, and there's no chance I am pregnant.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, pulse 92 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, temperature 36.8°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Awake, restless, and mildly disheveled young woman with psychomotor agitation, rapid body gestures, and intense, unblinking eye contact.

Alert and fully oriented; speech is rapid, loud, and pressured; mood is elevated and irritable; thought process reveals flight of ideas with grandiose themes, without hallucinations or suicidal ideation; insight is partial.
Skin is warm, pink, and dry with normal turgor, no rashes, and no intravenous needle tracks.
Pupils are equally round and reactive to light; extraocular movements are intact without exophthalmos or lid lag.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, non-tender, and moves freely on swallowing without palpable nodules or bruits.
Regular rhythm at 92 beats per minute with normal S1 and S2, and no murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally without wheezing, rales, or rhonchi.
Abdomen is soft, non-distended, and non-tender throughout with no palpable masses or hepatosplenomegaly.
Cranial nerves II through XII are grossly intact with symmetric facial movements and intact sensation.
Normal muscle tone and full 5/5 strength in all four extremities without focal weakness or cogwheel rigidity.
Deep tendon reflexes are 2+ and symmetric throughout, and plantar responses are flexor bilaterally.
No resting tremor, postural tremor, asterixis, or involuntary movements detected.
Neck is supple without nuchal rigidity, and Kernig and Brudzinski signs are negative.
Gait is brisk and energetic with steady balance, and finger-to-nose and rapid alternating movements are intact.
